speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. When did you deliver, and can you describe the nature and severity of your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a fever, and have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge? Also, are you experiencing any pain or burning sensation when you urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does your vaginal discharge have a foul odor, and have you noticed any red streaks or pus in your urine? I also need to know if you had any tears or an episiotomy during the delivery.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

text: Complains of minor difficulty in breathing but denies any urinary pain, headache, vomiting, or diarrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: The minor difficulty in breathing is concerning for a potential pulmonary embolism, so I will order imaging to rule that out. REQUEST TEST: CT Pulmonary Angiography, Lower Extremity Doppler Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the pulmonary embolism workup is negative, I am focusing on the uterine tenderness and fever which strongly suggest postpartum endometritis. REQUEST TEST: Endometrial Culture, Blood Cultures

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the negative cultures, your uterine tenderness and fever remain the primary clinical findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis
